# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshChallengeTracker`) renders the challenge panel as compact rows: indicator + title + description, with a `Challenges (n/N)` header. There is currently no per-challenge progress display.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps every challenge template 1:1 to a persistent Steam achievement; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- Add an `economic` challenge category and the `ch-serial-seller` template with an evaluator counting sold street businesses and an optional progress provider.
- Add an optional `progress?: (state: MainStreetState) => { current: number; target: number }` field to the `Challenge` interface and render it in the challenge HUD tracker (e.g. `2/3`), leaving progress-less challenges visually unchanged.
- Add the `serial-seller` achievement mapping and create the blocking dependency work item for the `core` manifest entry + Steamworks API name.
- Update the affected tests (template count, evaluator/selection/progress/undo, achievement mapping) and documentation.

Design note: keeping progress as an **optional Main Street-specific** field on `Challenge` (rather than extending the generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` in `@core-engine`) keeps the change surgical and avoids touching the core engine. If a second progress-capable challenge is added later, promoting the field to the generic interface can be revisited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add `economic` to `ChallengeCategory`, add optional `progress` to `Challenge`, add the `ch-serial-seller` template (evaluator + progress).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render progress in `refreshChallengeTracker`.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` — add `'ch-serial-seller': 'serial-seller'` to `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`.
- `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — update template count (12 → 13); add evaluator, selection, and progress-metadata tests.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` — mapping completeness/drift now includes `serial-seller` (green once the child manifest entry lands).
- `tests/main-street/` challenge-HUD/scene test — add progress-rendering coverage (extend an existing scene/HUD test or add a focused one).
- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — **blocking dependency** `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (core submodule): add the `serial-seller` entry with `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and/or `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — document the new challenge/category if the challenge catalogue is described there.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — only if the progress indicator requires a layout constant tweak (avoid if possible).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Cross-repo achievement dependency (blocking, build impact).** The manifest lives in the `core` submodule and the drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) fails the build until the dependency (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`) lands and the submodule pointer is bumped. Sequence the dependency first; this item must not reach `in_review` ahead of it.
- **Test friction from template count.** Several tests derive from `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES.length`; only `challenges.test.ts` hardcodes 12. Keep the category-coverage list at the original 5 so `economic` is not required to have ≥2 templates (scope creep risk — do not add a second economic challenge here; capture as a separate linked work item).
- **Undo semantics.** Because completion is flagged on the `ActiveChallenge` and also recorded in `challengesCompleted`, redo must not double-add. Existing per-action reset (`completedChallengeIds.length = 0`) already guards this; add regression coverage.
- **Progress layout.** The challenge rows are compact; a progress suffix must not overlap the description column. Verify at the shipping HUD width.
- **Assumption:** `soldSlots` true-count is the intended "businesses sold" metric (confirmed by producer, Q6 = a). If a future non-street sell path should count, a state counter will be needed — out of scope.
- **Assumption:** final player-facing text is title **Serial Seller** and description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game." (producer-confirmed Q7 update); the `economic` category keeps the original 5-category coverage assertions intact.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding more economic challenges, changing reward points, adding new achievement art, or counting hand/legacy sells are out of scope; capture as linked work items.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04` (`Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements`, stage `plan_complete`) / `CG-0MUNC7FK5001T5CP` — established the 1:1 challenge→achievement mapping and drift guard this item extends.
- `CG-0MU37CKRR008252I` — per-action challenge evaluation (the path that completes this challenge after a sell).
- `CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC` / `CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV` — Sell vs Close mechanics (sold markers, undo snapshot/restore).
- `MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC` (`Main Street: verify capacity-stable HandView slots (bump core submodule …)`, completed/`in_review`) — precedent for bumping the `core` submodule pointer from a Main Street change, as the blocking dependency here will need to do.
- Automated related-work report — see the `
## Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL** – Add a charity shop (completed)
- **MS-0MUO7FS95000OLN9** – When adding a card to the market slot using the developer cheat menu can't take card (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Scope of "sell 3 businesses" — cumulative across the run or within a single turn?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) total businesses sold across the entire game run (cumulative).** Source: interactive reply, comment `MS-C0MUOE84S1001BB5M`.
- **Q2: Which challenge category?**
  - Answer (producer): **(c) create a new `economic` category** for buy/sell/space-management challenges. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Reward points?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) standard `CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`** (same as the existing 12). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: UI feedback — progress or title/description only?**
  - Answer (producer): **progress** (e.g. "2/3 businesses sold"). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: Persistent Steam achievement?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a)** map to a persistent Steam achievement, with the `core`-submodule manifest + Steamworks backend config split into a separate **blocking child** work item. Source: interactive reply, comment `MS-C0MUOHDERC008QLXL`. Research: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 12 templates 1:1; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, which is tracked in the `core` submodule (separate repo).
- **Q6: Which sale actions count?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) only street/tableau sales via Manage Card → Sell**, tracked by the existing `soldSlots` array; no new state counter. Source: interactive reply. Research: `sellBusiness` (`src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`) leaves sold cards on the grid and sets `soldSlots`; sold cards cannot be closed, so the count is monotonic and undo-aware.

# Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw)

**Summary:** Add the engine logic for the Investor's free market re-roll: per-turn state tracking, the bias-aware draw algorithm, and the integration with the existing market refill path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform one coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it advances the per-turn escalation counter (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a 75% chance to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space synergyTypes; event targetSynergy/effect; staff allowedBusinessTypes overlap with the hosting business's synergy types).
- The biased draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed produces same-game determinism.
- `refillSingleRowMarket` is parameterised to accept the bias/relevance pool; the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- The bias draw preserves the >=1-business row composition invariant.

**Parent Coverage:** Implements parent AC2 (One free re-roll per turn) and parent AC3 (Relevance bias).

**Minimal Implementation:**
- Add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` to state types
- Reset flag at `WeekStart`
- Implement `canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`
- Implement bias-aware draw in `refillSingleRowMarket`
- Wire up the bias detection (hosting business synergy types overlap)

**Dependencies:** Add Investor card to catalog (CSV + types + parsing)

**Deliverables:** Engine functions, state field, bias draw algorithm, WeekStart reset.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`

# Intake Brief: Re-evaluate Upgrade Costs/ROI After the Five-Turn Payback Rebalance

**Work item:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 (Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns)
**Recommendation R1:** Re-evaluate upgrade costs/incomeBonus so upgrades clear the ~5-turn payback opportunity cost.

## Headline

The five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3) left upgrades severely under-valued: 9 of 39 upgrade cards show 0% adoption on the after-state, and the expensive tier (cost 7–14) is universally rejected by the greedy AI. This task re-derives upgrade `cost` and `incomeBonus` values so upgrades are genuinely worth purchasing in a meaningful share of runs.

## Problem statement

Businesses now recover their cost in ~5 turns, making each turn of play more economically tense. However, an upgrade must (a) require a parent business to already be owned, and (b) spend 3–14 coins on top of the business's remaining payback, so upgrades rarely clear the opportunity cost before the run ends. With `incomeBonus` values set proportionally to upgrade cost (e.g. cost 9 → bonus 300), the ROI `incomeBonus × horizon − cost` is positive only when `horizon` is large — but runs last ~10–12 turns on average, and the AI's planning horizon (floor=5, cap=25) means cheap upgrades barely clear positive-NPV. The expensive tier never does.

## Users

- **Player** — wants building decisions to carry real economic tension, including meaningful upgrade choices (e.g. "Should I invest in my Diner or bank these coins?"). Currently, upgrades feel like dead ends.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a diverse economy where investment (upgrades) is a viable strategy alongside banking and business expansion.
- **Developer** — wants the changes to be small, targeted, and reversible, backed by before/after Monte Carlo evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** The current upgrade pick rate (M1: purchases / market appearances) and M5 adoption (upgrade purchases / parent purchases) are recorded from the after-state canonical profile (200 seeds, 60 max turns, `mc-balance`, greedy). Results documented in the work-item description.
2. **Changes applied.** Upgrade `cost` and/or `incomeBonus` values in `src/card-data.csv` are adjusted so that at least the cheap upgrades (cost ≤5) reach a measurable pick rate and the expensive tier reaches a non-trivial pick rate. **No engine-rule changes.**
3. **Before/after evidence.** The canonical Monte Carlo profile is re-run post-change; pick rates and adoption rates are recorded as a before/after comparison. Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard is preserved.
4. **Full test suite passes** with the new values (`npm test`).

> Standard criteria also met: at least one testing/validation criterion (AC2), documentation updated where relevant, and full suite green (AC4). CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- **No engine-rule changes** (card-data.csv is the only lever).
- **Integer ×100 economy** — costs and bonuses are integer coin-cent units.
- **Preserve the win-rate ladder** (Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard) as the primary gate.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Community-space pricing, event pricing, and business income are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline:** Changes must not materially shift win rates (±0.05 on Medium) — upgrades represent a small share of total income.

## Existing state

### Post-rebalance after-state (commit 8b8fe46, current dev tip — card-data unchanged since rebalance)

**200 seeds / 60 turns / Medium / greedy Monte Carlo (canonical profile):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs with ≥1 upgrade | 31.0% (62/200) |
| Aggregate M1 pick rate (all upgrades) | 8.18% (88/1076 appearances) |
| Upgrade share of all purchases | 8.43% (89/1056) |
| Aggregate M5 adoption (upgrade vs parent owns) | ~10.50% |

### Upgrade performance (after-state, sorted by M1 pick rate)

**Top performers (M1 ≥ 15%):**
| Upgrade | Cost | incomeBonus | M1 Pick Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upg-gourmet-truck | 3 | 150 | 24.0% |
| upg-gaming-lounge | 7 | 200 | 23.8% |
| upg-gourmet-deli | 4 | 150 | 19.2% |
| upg-bistro | 3 | 100 | 18.8% |
| upg-bespoke-tailor | 4 | 100 | 17.9% |

**Mid performers (M1 5–15%):**
upg-readers-cafe (17.4%), upg-patisserie (16.7%), upg-roastery (12.1%), upg-wellness-retreat (12.1%), upg-tea-lounge (12.0%), upg-resort-spa (11.5%), upg-smoothie-bar (11.5%), upg-grand-fountain (11.1%), upg-adventure-park (10.3%), upg-community-hub (9.4%), upg-vintage-shop (9.1%), upg-garden (8.7%), upg-orchard (8.7%)

**Low performers (M1 0–5%):**
upg-designer-store (7.7%), upg-fast-food (7.4%), upg-drive-in (7.1%), upg-fitness-center (6.7%), upg-garden-center (6.5%), upg-bread-factory (6.5%), upg-toy-warehouse (6.5%), upg-dry-cleaners (5.7%), upg-imax (4.8%), upg-health-center (3.7%), upg-wellness-center (3.2%), upg-private-medical-center (3.1%)

**Never picked (M1 = 0%):**
upg-home-improvement, upg-salon, upg-museum, upg-medical-center, upg-grand-bakehouse, upg-restaurant, upg-multiplex, upg-luxury-retreat, upg-dental-clinic (9 upgrades)

### AI upgrade scoring formula

```
score = incomeBonus × horizon − cost
horizon = clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score) / scorePace), 5, 25)
```

For a 0-turn-horizon floor of 5:
- Cost 3, bonus 100 → score = 500 − 300 = **+200** (positive, competitive)
- Cost 9, bonus 300 → score = 1500 − 900 = **+600** (positive at floor, but expensive)
- Cost 14, bonus 550 → score = 2750 − 1400 = **+1350** (positive but very high cost)

The expensive upgrades' high `incomeBonus` values make them look attractive on paper, but their high `cost` means they rarely appear in the market before the game ends, and when they do, the AI prioritises cheaper alternatives with better cost-adjusted returns.

## Desired change

1. **Raise `incomeBonus` or lower `cost` for the 0%-tier upgrades.** Target: lift the top cheap upgrades to ≥20% M1 pick rate and the expensive tier to ≥5% M1 pick rate.
2. **Adjust the cheap tier upward modestly** if they fall below the target.
3. **Document every change with rationale.**
4. **Re-run Monte Carlo and compare.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Upgrade row edits (`cost`, `incomeBonus`).
- `tests/main-street/business-payback.test.ts` — May need update if cost/income changes affect business payback (unlikely, as upgrades are a separate family).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/card-metrics.ts` — M5 `computeUpgradeAdoption` may need base-ID normalisation (instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` vs. base card IDs).
- `docs/main-street/` — Update balance documentation with before/after results.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns (parent context).
- **MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0** — Re-tune compensating balance levers (deferred upgrade pricing to this item).
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Further-balancing recommendations (R1: upgrade re-pricing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Premise nuance (research finding).** The "≤1% of runs" claim in the further-balancing report appears to refer to per-upgrade individual run-participation (many are ≤1%). However, the aggregate picture is more nuanced: 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade, and the cheap tier already shows 16–24% M1 pick rates. Only the expensive tier (cost 7–9+) is truly broken at 0%. This may narrow the scope.
- **Metric definition note.** The M1/M5 functions (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`) compare base card IDs against instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` entries (e.g., `biz-laundromat-1`). The baseline should either (a) normalise IDs by stripping `-N` suffixes or (b) use instance IDs consistently. This is a known pattern in `MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`.
- **No engine-rule changes.** Changes are card-data only; the scoring formula and horizon remain unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk.** If producer wants community-space or event pricing adjustments too, record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline.** Upgrade income is a small share of total income, so changes should have minimal impact on overall win rates. The win-rate ladder should be preserved.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (success metric & scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is the success threshold, and which upgrade tiers need fixing?*
  - **Recommended: B** — Focus on the expensive tier (cost ≥7) where 9 upgrades hit 0% adoption. Cheap upgrades already perform at 16–24% M1.
  - Option A: Fix all upgrades, target ≥5% M1 for every upgrade.
  - Option B: Fix only expensive tier (cost ≥7), target ≥5% M1.
  - Option C: Accept current cheap-tier performance; only fix expensive tier to ≥10% M1.

  **Answer (producer):** B- **Q2 (change scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is in bounds for changes?*
  - **Recommended: A** — `cost` + `incomeBonus` in card-data.csv only.
  - Option A: Cost + incomeBonus only.
  - Option B: Also adjust AI horizon parameters (AI_HORIZON_FLOOR, scoring formula).
  - Option C: Also adjust guardrail preservation requirements.

  **Answer (producer):** A- **Q3 (premise accuracy — OPEN QUESTION):** *The data shows 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade (aggregate M1 = 8.18%). The "≤1% of runs" claim in the report refers to per-upgrade individual participation. Should the goal be to lift ALL upgrades above the current floor, or only the broken tier?*
  - **Recommended: B** — The expensive tier (9 upgrades at 0%) is the real problem; cheap upgrades already meet a reasonable baseline.

  **Answer (producer):** B
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).

None needed — straightforward resource mutation.

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.
- **Fallback.** When no conditions match, the option's `successorId` is used.
- **All boundary cases tested.** Above/below threshold, equality boundary (`==`), and no-match fallback.
- **Successor-card push.** The matched successor is pushed via `pushChainCard` as before.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` push `successorId` as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Update `resolveStorylineOption` to evaluate conditional successors.

## Deliverables

- Conditional successor evaluation logic.
- Unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

None needed — pure predicate evaluation.

## Goal

A content designer can run `npm run storylines:editor` and see the committed
storyline graph rendered from `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`, with
storyline grouping, choice-card distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom and node
selection. Read-only in this slice — no writes.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
understand an arc before changing it."

## Scope

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — `vite-node` entry point with `--help`,
  `--port` and `--host`; boots the editor host and exits 0 on `--help`.
- Editor host serving the dev page via a dedicated `vite.editor.config.ts`
  (the root `vite.config.ts` is auto-generated and must not be hand-edited).
- `view-model.ts` — pure loader/mapper from the manifest (keys `version`,
  `source`, `storylineIds`, `nodes`, `edges`, `cycles`) to a render-ready view
  model (nodes, edges, storyline groups, choice flags, cycle flags).

## Goal

Edits from the editor are routed through the existing transactional author API,
previewed and validated before writing, with committed artefacts regenerated and
a concurrency guard preventing lost updates.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want an edit to be previewed and validated before it
is written, so I cannot write a dangling chain or clobber someone else's edit."

## Scope

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — thin bridge over the existing modules,
  reusing their exported functions:
  - `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — `parseCsv`, `addCard`, `linkCard`,
    `applyToFile`, `parseAuthorArgs` (`add-card` / `link` / `set-storyline`).
  - `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — `validateStorylines`,
    `formatStorylineReport`, `storylineReportToJson`.
  - `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — `buildStorylineManifest`,
    `serializeManifest`, `renderMermaid`.
  Expose `previewEdit`, `validateEdit`, `applyEdit`, `regenerateArtefacts`.
- Editor host API endpoints (same Vite/`vite-node` toolchain so the `?raw` CSV
  import resolves) for preview / validate / apply.
- Diff/preview response: before/after CSV rows for the affected card(s) plus the
  validation report.
- Concurrency guard: content hash (or mtime) of `src/card-data.csv` captured at
  load, compared before any write; on mismatch refuse and instruct a reload.
- Artefact regeneration after an accepted edit (write `storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `storyline-manifest.json`), keeping generators deterministic/timestamp-free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every edit returns a preview/diff and runs the validator before writing; an
  invalid edit exits non-zero, leaves `src/card-data.csv` byte-identical, and
  surfaces the offending card/link.
- After an accepted edit, `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` are regenerated;
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format json --check` and
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` pass.
- If `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load, the bridge refuses to write
  and returns a reload instruction (unit test).
- No editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through
  `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`; the T1 write-path guard passes.
- A round-trip test on a fixture proves a valid edited fixture validates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — **new** author/validator/graph bridge.
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` — **new** host API endpoints.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/bridge.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/preview-validate.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/concurrency.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Write bridge, host API endpoints, preview/diff payload, concurrency guard,
  artefact regeneration, unit tests.

## Goal

Authors can edit existing card fields and add/relink a card through guided forms
that show a diff preview and inline validation before committing.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor links
in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a dangling
chain."

## Scope

- Edit form for existing card fields: `name`, effect text, coin/reputation
  deltas, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
  `storylineTitle`.
- Guided "add card" form that creates a card and links it into a storyline
  (`addCard` + `linkCard` through the F2 bridge).
- Preview panel showing the pending diff; inline validation errors that block
  the write.
- Discard pending (unwritten) changes before committing, leaving the CSV
  untouched.
- Wire the forms to the F2 bridge (`previewEdit` / `validateEdit` / `applyEdit`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The editor edits every field listed above; a round-trip test proves the edit
  validates and is written through the author API.
- The add-card form creates a card and links it into a storyline.
- Pending (unwritten) changes can be discarded before committing, leaving the
  CSV byte-identical.
- A preview/diff is shown before each accepted edit; validation errors surface
  inline and block the write.
- A browser test drives a representative edit round-trip on a fixture.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/tools/storyline-editor/edit-forms.ts` — **new** card field/edit forms.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/add-card-form.ts` — **new** guided add/link form.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/preview-panel.ts` — **new** diff + validation panel.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/edit-forms.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/edit-roundtrip.browser.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Card edit forms, add-card form, preview/diff panel, discard-changes support,
  unit + browser round-trip tests.

## Goal

Authors can create or rename a storyline group and reassign member cards through
the editor, driven through the same transactional author API (`set-storyline`).

## Scope

- Storyline list view (the five shipped storylines plus any created in-session),
  derived from the manifest's `storylineIds` and node `storylineId` /
  `storylineTitle`.
- Create a new `storylineId` / `storylineTitle` group.
- Rename an existing group and retitle it.
- Reassign member cards to a group.
- All operations route through the F2 bridge and validate before write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a storyline group, renaming one, and reassigning member cards all
  route through `set-storyline` and validate before write.
- The storyline list reflects the manifest after an accepted edit.
- Tests cover create/rename/reassign against a fixture CSV without mutating the
  committed CSV.
- The T1 write-path guard still passes (no second CSV write path is introduced).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/storyline-manager.test.ts` — **new**.

## Goal

Document the visual storyline editor for content designers and developers, and
run the final full-suite regression sweep once all editor features have landed.

## Context

`tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` pins the canonical doc
structure: headings `## 1. Concepts` … `## 10. Roadmap`, the five CSV columns,
the tooling commands (`validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph`,
`storylines:author`), and cross-references from `src/README.md` and
`docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`. New editor documentation
must extend those sections **without breaking the pinned headings or the drift
guard**.

## Scope

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — document `npm run storylines:editor`
  (launch), the read-only viewer, the edit workflow, preview/validation,
  artefact regeneration and storyline management, within the existing §5
  (Tooling) and §7 (Authoring walkthrough) structure.
- `src/README.md` — reference the `storylines:editor` script alongside the
  existing script/column references.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — reference the editor
  where the authoring workflow is described, if needed.
- Accurate code comments on the new editor modules.
- Final full-suite regression sweep, including the doc-drift and storylines
  tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` documents `npm run storylines:editor`, the
  viewer, the edit workflow, validation and artefact regeneration.
- `src/README.md` references the editor script and any new fields.
- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` passes with the updated docs
  (pinned headings and cross-references intact).
- New editor modules carry accurate doc comments.
- `npm test` (full unit suite) and the browser suite pass with the editor
  changes; the storyline regression harness stays green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/README.md` — **edit** script and column references.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — **edit** if needed.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-regression-harness.test.ts` — **verify** stays green.

## Deliverables
